operations.value:
A relic is a new kind of record in Workbook, separate from tasks. It holds specs, plans, decisions, transcripts and similar material, with the same history and sharing that tasks have. A relic has a title, a type, an author, links, and content made of named parts.

Relics can already link to tasks. This story lets a relic or part link to another relic or to one part of it, with an optional finer pointer.

The workflow this is built for: a meeting transcript is stored as a relic with one part per speaker turn. Decisions drawn from it are a second relic whose parts link back to the turns they came from. Each decision links on to the part of the spec it changes, and the spec's parts link to the tasks that build them.

## The link

```json
{ "id": "01M9…L",
  "from": "<part of this relic, or omitted for the whole relic>",
  "to": { "relic": "WB-R-01M8…", "part": "01M8…C" },
  "rel": "decided-in",
  "pointer": { "quote": "we agreed to compact by hand", "at": "00:14:32" } }
```

- A link starts from a relic or one of its parts. It points at a task, a relic, or a part of a relic.
- A link is stored once, on the relic it starts from. Nothing is written on the other end.
- **Pointer:** a link may carry an optional pointer inside its target part, such as a quote or a timestamp. The project's schema defines its shape. Workbook stores it and does not interpret it. It is at most 512 bytes.
- The target must exist when the link is added. If it is later removed, retired or deleted, the link stays and is shown as pointing at something removed or retired.
- A link points at its target as it is now. History can show whether the target changed after the link was made.
- Links are within one project. A link to another project is refused.
- Concurrent adds and removes all survive.

## Following a link from both ends

- The index keeps relic and part targets searchable by either end. "What points at this part?" is one lookup, with no crawl and no background job.
- `relic update <relic> --link <relic>[#part] [--from <part>] --rel R [--pointer '{…}']`.
- `relic show <relic>[#part]` lists links going out and links coming in.
- `relic list --linked-to <relic>[#part]`.

## Done when

- The transcript, decision and spec chain above can be built from the command line and followed in both directions.
- Rebuilding the index restores every reverse lookup.
- A link to a removed part or a deleted relic is shown as removed and fails no command.
- A link to a relic that this clone has not fetched yet is handled without an error.
- Re-running the relic benchmark shows the link lookup target still holds.

## Where the design is

This story builds the part "Links" of the design relic WB-R-01M8EVZ9BQR7GNFYPYHSVT6FRC, part 01M8EVZ9BQYSPW3MMGCB36ARJD.

Read it with `workbook relic show 'WB-R-01M8EVZ9BQR7GNFYPYHSVT6FRC#01M8EVZ9BQYSPW3MMGCB36ARJD' --body`.
